Replay

P2P party setup

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Signaling serviceCurrent game coverage

P2P_Party stores enrollment through Party, then registers the process for a P2P match whose player roster is fixed. It returns an authenticated match descriptor and WebRTC configuration. The game owns the runner that advances simulation; this helper neither creates an authority Room nor drives gameplay.

  1. Open P2P_Party with a Party_Config and the game's required player count. Use Player invites with invite_uses = players - 1. Checkpoint publication is an authority operation and must be disabled. Browser storage uses IndexedDB; native callers supply the existing Party_Storage adapter.
  2. Pump p2p_party_frame until party.recent_loaded. Call p2p_party_begin with Create, Join plus a parsed ticket, or Rejoin. The existing journal persists the request, grant and recent-room selection. A creator's party.code becomes shareable before other participants have enrolled.
  3. Continue pumping. After enrollment, the owner opens a separate control connection, obtains a fresh nonce using Godot Crypto, performs Challenge/Rebind, then queries until the entire enabled roster exists. This path creates no gameplay authority lease; the fixed-roster P2P protocol governs gameplay.
  4. When ready, obtain p2p_party_rtc. Keep the owner at its stable address while RTC borrows its authorization/ICE callbacks. The first roster member creates signaling; other members join. Supply the returned match scope and ordered roster to the P2P runner, and bind physical connections only after checking authenticated member identities. A transport ID is not a simulation player ID.
  5. Close gameplay transports before p2p_party_close, then close borrowed native storage. Close/reopen the owner to retry a failed enrollment/registration.

The lower-level replay/p2p/provision.Client supports non-Godot drivers. It takes an enrollment grant, required count, cryptographic per-process nonce, clock and transport. It registers an incarnation, waits for complete membership, and returns the match plus the local credential through client_admission. It retains the durable grant unchanged, so a new process can reuse the original stored grant and register a newer incarnation. Roster queries continue every 500 ms, with the same nonce and monotonically increasing sequence. Unanswered requests fail after ten seconds; they do not expose a speculative registration result.

The high-level owner requires a connected control socket within ten seconds. Errors clear readiness and are explicit through failed, the underlying Party and registration state, and p2p_party_message. It does not close an already running game on a control error. The embedding game chooses that policy. Duel continues established P2P gameplay if registration control becomes unavailable; it requires fresh registration for a future process. Automatic control reconnection after readiness is not implemented here.

Signaling service#

P2P_Rendezvous_Hub connects a bounded provisioning Hub to a WebSocket server. Route binary packets to the P2P provisioning/control entry points and text packets to p2p_rendezvous_hub_receive. Poll the socket once and pump the signaling hub each frame. The first text message chooses a current opaque room code; per-room challenge/MAC verification still decides admission. Rooms always use a mesh.

A guest may finish enrollment before the creator starts signaling. P2P party RTC configuration enables wait_for_host for guests: an explicit no_room reply can retry on a fresh socket after 500 ms, bounded by the original 15-second deadline. Authentication, malformed-protocol and other errors are not converted into retries. Existing signaling continuation behavior remains separate.

Current game coverage#

Duel uses this owner for browser create/join/rejoin. Its separate service combines private SQLite enrollment and challenged mesh signaling. Browser return still requires a compatible participant archive: room credentials do not contain the simulation or input history.

The native P2P Direct owner supplies authenticated two-player ENet gameplay, endpoint discovery and connection replacement. Party keeps registration and pair provisioning on separate Router lanes of one socket; p2p_party_pair_begin is also available to custom transport owners. Its endpoint is registered from the current configuration, allowing a returning process to change ports without rewriting the durable enrollment request.

Account/device transfer, public deployment, and broader outage recovery are outside the tested scope described here. ENet and browser WebRTC are separate gameplay backends; native RTC requires an appropriate extension.
